title: A Sum-of-Squares Hierarchy with Quadratic Convergence for Quantum Channel Coding
abstract: Computing the optimal success probability for transmitting classical messages through a single use of a quantum channel is NP-hard, even for two messages. An existing semidefinite programming hierarchy based on symmetric extensions provides convergent upper bounds with an a priori error estimate that decays as the inverse square root of the extension level. In this work, we construct a Hermitian sum-of-squares hierarchy for an arbitrary number of messages and prove quadratic convergence in its level. The error bound is proportional to the advantage over random guessing. Our approach combines state-discrimination duality with positive polynomial kernels on products of spheres to construct feasible polynomial dual certificates. For binary messages, the resulting bounds give a multiplicative approximation from above of the trace-norm contraction coefficient.
summary: This work develops a novel Hermitian Sum-of-Squares (SOS) hierarchy to provide upper bounds on the optimal success probability for quantum channel coding. By employing advanced techniques involving positive polynomial kernels, the authors prove that this hierarchy exhibits quadratic convergence, significantly improving upon existing error estimates. This provides a powerful, computationally tractable tool for analyzing fundamental limits in quantum communication theory.
main_problem: The paper addresses the NP-hard problem of computing the optimal success probability for transmitting classical messages through a single use of a quantum channel.
main_result: The authors construct a Hermitian Sum-of-Squares (SOS) hierarchy that achieves quadratic convergence for bounding this success probability.
method: The approach combines state-discrimination duality with positive polynomial kernels on products of spheres to construct feasible polynomial dual certificates for the SOS hierarchy.
model_or_system: The system involves a quantum channel $\Phi: L(A) 	o L(B)$ acting on finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces, where the goal is to maximize the average success probability $P_{	ext{succ}}(\Phi, k)$.
key_observables: Optimal success probability $P_{	ext{succ}}(\Phi, k)$ and the trace-norm contraction coefficient $\eta_{	ext{tr}}(\Phi)$.
important_parameters: The level $L$ of the hierarchy, and the dimension parameters $d_A$ and $d_B$ of the input and output spaces.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the structure of the sphere ideal and the use of positive squared-polynomial kernels to establish the convergence rate.
figures_summary: Figure 1 summarizes the construction, contrasting the SOS hierarchy with the feasible certificates used for convergence analysis.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the NP-hard problem and existing SDP bounds, to introducing the novel Hermitian SOS hierarchy, and finally proving the quadratic convergence rate using advanced polynomial and kernel techniques.
why_interesting: The development of polynomial-time, rapidly converging mathematical tools (SOS hierarchies) to solve fundamental, hard problems in quantum information theory is highly relevant for theoretical quantum physicists.
